html:
President Trump has announced the cancellation of planned strikes on Iran, stating his decision is subject to the rapid making of a deal. This development comes amid media reports of intense strikes being planned for the weekend and after the Saudi Crown Prince reportedly raised concerns over such actions, with Iran having warned of a "decisive response" to any aggression.

Middle East Tensions: Despite the cancelled strikes, high tensions persist in the Middle East, with US embassies urging citizens to consider departing the region. Iran’s Ghalibaf revealed details following Khamenei’s killing, while its Foreign Ministry stated Iran would use all means for legitimate defense. Meanwhile, Trump announced an agreement for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas, with him stating Israel is "very happy" with the Gaza disarmament agreement. However, Hamas has indicated that Israel’s commitment to stopping the killing of Palestinians is a prerequisite for a disarmament plan, and Israel says it won't withdraw until full demilitarization. Drone attacks continue to impact the region, with Jordan, Syria, Qatar, and Palestine condemning a drone strike on vessels at Egypt's Damietta Port, though Egypt denies such an attack occurred. Separately, anger is rising as ICC member states are accused of facilitating the flight of the Israeli prime minister to Washington.

Russia-Ukraine & European Security: Russian forces launched an overnight barrage on Kyiv, killing nine, with air defenses reportedly struggling and President Trump walking back a promised boost to Ukraine's missile defense systems. Russia also struck targets in Ukraine's Odesa and Mykolaiv ports, rattling global grain markets. Domestically, three people were killed and more than 20 injured after a bomb carried by a woman detonated at a Moscow restaurant. In a separate development highlighting ongoing sanctions evasion, a Russian ship defied sanctions to send military vehicles, including armoured personnel carriers, to Mali via the English Channel.

European Migration Crisis: Europe is grappling with a significant migration crisis after tens of thousands of people crossed from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, with reports indicating at least 67 deaths. Spain has installed a floating barrier and slammed "selfish" EU partners, as a majority of EU countries call for emergency talks. The Ceuta crossings have exposed deep divisions over migration, creating a political storm across Europe.

Global Economy & Market Impacts: Capital One announced it closed the Trump Organization’s accounts years ago after an anti-money-laundering review, marking the first time a bank has formally tied money-laundering concerns to Trump’s family business. Also in US economic news, Wall Street traders can now access Trump’s "Truth API" service for $100,000 a month to gain high-speed access to his economic policy and global affairs announcements. In other economic news, Hungary faces a potential power crunch as its sole nuclear plant is forced offline due to record-low water levels on the Danube. Across Southeast Asia, illegal cryptocurrency miners are reportedly stealing vast amounts of electricity, straining national grids and exposing links to organized crime.

International Incidents & Social Trends: Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja and his nine climbing companions were killed by an avalanche in Pakistan while attempting to climb one of the tallest peaks. In Peru, a tourist plane carrying foreign tourists crashed near the Nazca Lines archaeological site, killing all 13 people on board. Across West Africa, campaigners warn of a rise in anti-LGBTQ+ laws, with Senegal and Niger recently strengthening such legislation. Elsewhere, Europe is seeing a rise in "violence-as-a-service" tactics from networks like the Foxtrot Network, thought to be responsible for approximately 35 murders using teenage hitmen.
